messages.subject: RE: Follow-up: Dynr on RStudio Server Pro
messages.subject_clean: Follow-up: Dynr on RStudio Server Pro
messages.body_plain:
Thanks so much, Matt and Daniel. I just tested it and using R 4.0.5 works but the default R v4.1. crashes the session at the plotting stage as you said.

I am cc’ing the dynr team just so that we know. As far as I am aware, the dynr on CRAN was tested under Rv4.1 and the plotting was fine there. So I think it is just a matter of re-installing the ggplot packages into Rv4.1 on the server.

I would love to hear more about using Rstudio Cloud. Is it free for now and how can we get started?

Thanks!

Sy-Miin

From: Hansen, Matt <ma...@psu.edu>
Sent: Saturday, August 28, 2021 12:48 PM
To: Chow, Sy-Miin <qu...@psu.edu>
Cc: Kuwahara, Daniel Toshiro <dt...@psu.edu>
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dynr on RStudio Server Pro

Hi Sy-Miin,

Thank you for the demo file.

Some good news that the dynr.cook() function should now run successfully.  I believe the resource limits were preventing this from completing.

There is currently an issue with ggplot2(), which causes the plotting at the end of the demo to also crash R. Our version of RStudio needs to be updated to properly support R v4.1. Daniel and I will work together to either update RStudio or change the default R version back to 4.0.5. As a workaround you can use the dropdown in the upper right to switch to R 4.0.5. All the packages in /courses/HDFS538 were built with R 4.1.0 so the typical warning messages will appear but the demo ran successfully for me. This library can be rebuilt with R 4.0.5 if you prefer, depending on the decision to upgrade RStudio, or you can continue to use the DynamicalSystems library.

The new version of RStudio Server introduced a lot of new changes so it may be problematic to upgrade since the semester has started but we will try it out.

https://blog.rstudio.com/2021/06/09/rstudio-v1-4-update-whats-new/ <https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.rstudio.com%2F2021%2F06%2F09%2Frstudio-v1-4-update-whats-new%2F&data=04%...%40psu.edu%7C1f6401895d0b4d4befc108d96a4396b9%7C7cf48d453ddb4389a9c1c115526eb52e%7C0%7C0%7C637657660780123189%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C1000&sdata=EsUkEfImZnyPovzC5bJtpCM1BTHiIjOlc5qEea7WJLU%3D&reserved=0>

As a side note, I tested dynr on RStudio Cloud (http://rstudio.cloud <https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Frstudio.cloud%2F&data=04%...%40psu.edu%7C1f6401895d0b4d4befc108d96a4396b9%7C7cf48d453ddb4389a9c1c115526eb52e%7C0%7C0%7C637657660780123189%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C1000&sdata=6n0NpZbA8hZCbSAxaM1iehji1WTIAetA3Dv990AC9h8%3D&reserved=0>) and it installed relatively quickly and the demo ran successfully. Using Cloud might be an alternative for you. There’s still no formal university agreement in place for the paid tiers but I know Daniel and his group plans to continue to work on it.

- Matt
